note: case lists (a chain of `Case` tokens ending on the `0xffff` terminator)
testable arms, i.e. every case of every list but the terminator
terminator cases, each opening a `default:` body
the shortest arm body, in statements
mean arm length, in tenths of a statement
arms with no body at all -- the shared `case A: case B:` shape
arms whose first statement is a `JumpIfNot`, i.e. the source's own `if` at the head of the arm
arms that leave through a `Jump` landing on their list's end
arms that leave through a `Jump` landing somewhere else (`continue`, or out of a loop)
arms whose last `Jump` is a loop's own back edge (its target is behind it), so the arm runs on into the next case's code once the loop ends
arms whose last statement read as a token because a `Return`'s operand is a token of its own in the statement stream
arms that stop with no jump and a case still after them, i.e. they run into the next case's code
arms that stop with no jump as their list's last arm, i.e. they run into the `default:` body
lists whose `break` jumps all land on one offset -- the switch's end
lists whose arm jumps disagree, so the end is not one offset
lists with no `break` jump at all
`default:` bodies whose end no `break` names, so the extent stops at the script's end
bodies (an arm or a `default:`) carrying a `Switch` of their own
lists with a single arm, where the body's end is the terminator itself
arms whose case value is a `ByteConst`
arms whose case value is a compact integer token (`IntConstByte`, `IntZero`, `IntOne`, `IntConst`)
arms whose case value is a `StringConst`
arms whose case value is a `NameConst`
arms whose case value is an expression the compiler emitted (`InstanceVariable`, `PrimitiveCast`, ...)
